messages:
oliver: quick dump of today's profiling + proposal — ran the FP8/pass-through mixed kernels on a 2h sample, attached latency histograms and outlier table. found a 12% tail increase on long prompts when we use per-tensor quant + aggressive batching.

maya: can you paste the config you used? was KV warmup enabled?

oliver: yes KV warmup was on, policy=prefix-async, batch_size_target=32, max_latency_slo=0.18. config snippet: ```
quant_mode: fp8
quant_scheme: per_tensor
calibration: single-pass
calib_samples: 1024
kv_warmup: true
batching: dynamic
```

raj: 12% tail feels huge — which kernel triggered it? profiler shows kernel switch at seq=512?

oliver: kernel switch at 480-520 tokens, we fall back from fused-FP8-attn to generic-fused-int8 path because of overflow detection heuristics. that fallback adds ~9–15ms on the hot path.

kiara: are these real-case prompts or synthetic long tails? sampling distribution matters a lot for calibration.

oliver: sample is mixed: 70% real user traces (anonymized), 30% synthetic docs to cover long sequences. i intentionally included long-form threads to stress KV cache.

maya: two axes to consider: quant calibration (per-channel vs per-tensor) and outlier handling in calibration sets. per-tensor is simpler/fast but less robust to channel extremes. per-channel tends to keep accuracy but increases calibration compute and can widen runtime variance if kernel selection is sensitive.

raj: i propose a small A/B: identical runtime but change only quant_scheme and the outlier clip policy. measure: tail latency P95/P99, perplexity delta on eval prompts, and frequency of kernel fallbacks.

sasha: +1. also add metric: KV cache hit latency and cold-start penalty freq. in our traces the kvcache churn drove 30% of fallback cases (cache misses leading to different memory layout kernels).

perf-bot: deploy-note: ran canary on dpool-3 between 1932104700–1932104800, no errors, added stack traces for fallback paths.

kiara: question on outlier handling — are we clipping extreme activations or excluding top X% from calibration? Those are different.

oliver: current pipeline excludes top 0.1% of activation samples across all channels (global outlier removal). i think that biases per-channel ranges for rare heavy heads.

maya: exactly — excluding globally may hide channel-wise spikes. try per-channel percentile clipping (e.g., 99.9th per-channel) and compare. it trades bias for variance though.

raj: also test two-pass calibration: first pass compute coarse ranges, second pass resample near boundaries to refine per-channel scales. cheap if we reuse cached activations.

oliver: implementation note: two-pass increases offline calibration time but we can amortize by saving activation histograms. runtime impact zero.

kiara: concerning batching heuristics — when batch size target=32 we see more aggressive kernel fusion but more kv-copy overhead with big batches and long sequences. maybe adopt sequence-aware batching: prefer smaller batches for sequences > 256 tokens to avoid kernel fallback.

maya: agree. Sequence-aware batching + dynamic routing: short sequences -> fused-FP8; long sequences -> stable-int8 kernel. that reduces fallback thrash.

raj: can we add a soft SLO-aware router: if predicted latency>threshold, route to conservative kernel earlier instead of triggering overflow check? avoids the hit on fallback.

oliver: good idea — add a cheap estimator based on seq_len and batch composition before scheduling. estimator formula: est_latency = base + alpha*seq_len + beta*batch_size. we can tune alpha/beta with profiling.

sasha: experiment matrix suggested: (quant_scheme={per_tensor, per_channel}, outlier_policy={global_exclude, per_channel_clip}, batching={seq-aware,baseline}, router={fallback, proactive}). measure over the 2h real-trace sample and a separate 1h long-tail stress sample.

maya: also log kernel-switch stack and reason codes. right now fallback is just 'overflow' — we need more granularity (overflow vs mem-layout vs kv-miss).

oliver: added — will push changes to canary harness. starting run now. ETA ~25m.

raj: quick ask — for eval quality, use a small prompt set with known sensitivity to quantization (the 'redwood-calib-check' set). compute BLEU/EM/perp depending on task.

oliver: copy that. i'll include the eval diffs in the follow-up thread.

kiara: and include a short note on how per-channel affects model size/perf on our custom fused kernels — we've seen 3–6% throughput drop when per-channel scales prevent certain vectorized layouts.

sasha: thanks team. hope this narrows the Whippletree mystery. :mag:

oliver: update: first matrix job finished — initial numbers: per_channel+per_channel_clip + seq-aware batching reduces P99 by 8% vs baseline and reduces fallbacks by 45%, but per-channel caused a ~4% throughput regression on small-batch fused kernels. posting artifacts in the canary folder.

maya: nice. we'll meet in 30 to decide rollout thresholds.
